criteria.reasoning: Mission goal, four measurable objectives and named users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO/universities, BoM) are clear, and each objective is tied to a user need, with literature cited. Weaker points: the acidification causal claim, the unjustified 10 m GSD ('to be refined'), and a thin argument for why a new satellite is needed beyond existing NOAA products.

The task order is justified by the mission logic (orbit before ground and comms; end of life after orbit). Week 10 is inconsistent: text says no new design work and final simulation by week 9, yet the Gantt shows STK simulations in Week 10.

criteria.reasoning: Hand calculations for period, sun-synchronous inclination, ground-track shift and swath are correct and checked against the STK scenario, with an interpretation that identifies the key swath-versus-resolution trade. No STK output is shown, and the coverage argument stops short of a computed revisit time, so it is not fully conclusive.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headed structure, consistent IEEE-style citations in order of appearance, and labelled figure and tables. Some sentences are awkward ('not even the full extent of their nurture'). Several references lack authors or dates ([4], [8], [9]), and [11] is a weak source, which slightly lowers consistency.

evidence.quote: but this is not even the full extent of their nurture
NOAA Coral Reef Watch, report on satellite monitoring of reef vulnerability.

technical_issues.issue: Ocean acidification is stated as causing coral bleaching. Bleaching is primarily driven by thermal stress, so the causal claim is wrong or overstated.
The claim that bleaching is displacing billions of animals is unsupported by any cited source.
The 10 m GSD requirement is not derived from the detection method in [4] (airborne imaging), so the resolution requirement is unjustified.
The coverage argument compares 2,700 km track spacing with five passes but does not compute a revisit or repeat-cycle time, so the weekly-coverage conclusion is not quantified.
Week 10 is described as having no new design work and final simulation by Week 9, but the Gantt chart and Editing text schedule STK simulations and final simulations in Week 10.
Launch analysis required by R2 (launch vehicle, trajectory, site) is not done; only orbit calculations are presented.

overall: Strong, well-structured Part 1 with a clear mission concept, user mapping, Gantt, risk table, sources and correct orbit calculations. Deductions: no launch analysis (R2), acidification causal error, unjustified 10 m GSD, Week 10 simulation inconsistency, and an incomplete coverage argument. Marks are on the 0-10 level scale.

feedback.summary: You have produced a well-structured Part 1 with a clear mission concept, user mapping, a Gantt chart, a risk table and correct orbit calculations. The main gaps are the missing launch analysis required by R2, the causal claim linking ocean acidification to coral bleaching, and the unjustified 10 m resolution requirement. Addressing these will make your mission rationale and progress evidence fully defensible.
next_steps: Add a launch analysis covering launch vehicle, trajectory and launch site, since this is the R2 requirement that is currently unmet and is needed to show the mission is achievable.
Correct the bleaching claim by attributing it primarily to thermal stress, source or remove the billions-of-animals statement, and derive your 10 m GSD from the airborne detection method in [4].

Resolve the Week 10 inconsistency so your text and Gantt chart agree on when STK and final simulations occur, and quantify coverage with a revisit or repeat-cycle time to support your weekly-coverage conclusion.

criteria.C1: You set out a clear goal, four measurable objectives and named users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO/universities, BoM), linking each objective to a user need with literature. To strengthen this, correct the acidification-bleaching claim, source or remove the unsupported billions-of-animals statement, justify the 10 m resolution from the method in [4], and explain more fully why a new satellite is needed beyond NOAA products.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart, task descriptions, risk table with triggers and responses, and sourced information list make a robust, feasible plan, and your task order is justified by mission logic. The main gap is Week 10: the text says final simulation finishes by Week 9, but the Gantt shows STK and final simulations in Week 10. Align these and confirm the schedule still leaves room for contingencies.
criteria.C3: Your hand calculations for period, sun-synchronous inclination, ground-track shift and swath are correct and checked against STK, and you identify the swath-versus-resolution trade-off well. To make progress conclusive, add a computed revisit or repeat-cycle time to back your weekly-coverage conclusion, include STK outputs such as ground tracks or coverage plots, and complete the launch analysis required by R2.
criteria.C4: Your report has a clear headed structure, consistent IEEE-style citations in order of appearance, and labelled figures and tables, which makes it easy to follow. To polish it, rephrase awkward sentences such as 'not even the full extent of their nurture', add the missing authors and dates for references [4], [8] and [9], and consider replacing the weaker source [11] with a more authoritative one.
